messages.subject: RE: Question about large files [SEC=UNOFFICIAL]
parts:
G’day

 

I had thought that with R, the computers memory was one of the main limitations, is it possible to increase the virtual memory on the machine ?

 

 

If you can you could try to stratify your sample to build your models. If you could ensure that your highest value and lowest value of each variable is included in the sample, and then a random sample of at least 10% is included then you should be able to build a functioning representative sample. If however you could work out your stratifications and ensure that each stratification included the Min and Max, and then a proportional random sample for that specific stratification, which would give you a stronger representation.

 

If you decide to split or transform your database, then you need to be sure that the variable names are consistent across the modelling set and the scoring set as well. The scoring process wont work if the names are different.

 

As far as restrictions on model sizes, I don’t know the answer to that. Sorry

 

Regards

Tony

 

 

 

 

 

From: rattle...@googlegroups.com [mailto:rattle...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Richard Palmer
Sent: Friday, 15 August 2008 06:14
To: rattle...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Question about large files

 

If I have a file that is too large for memory (by lots), What is the right way to handle it through rattle.  To me, there appear to be two separate issues:  sampling for analysis and the data from the developed model.  What preliminary work do I have to do on the file to sample it?  If I say to score using the developed model, will Rattle score the resulting file without complaint.  If the file is too big for memory, are certain models restricted from use?
